objects.original: Eq. (15) uses the actual degree sum of entrywise ordered tensor contractions in the joint coefficient direct sum. Eq. (16) multiplies this angular field by the radial product to form H_i at the fixed location.
objects.reconstructed: The full coordinate set is a disjoint union over level-degree pairs of coordinate assignments to ordered repeated tensor slots. The angular field uses the unscaled restriction of the same draw to each (i,p) block, and the radial field uses the product c or its explicit zero extension.
objects.evidence: For a level k the dependent repetition slots have size S_k and adding a copy index of size p gives p S_k slots; all choices of basis index give exactly n^(p S_k) ordered coordinates. Multiplying the entries of the matching u_j yields precisely the corresponding coordinate of the repeated source tensor. WithLp.toLp 2 is the Euclidean wrapper, not a scaling or new draw. Taking the degree sum first and multiplying by c gives the sum of the radial components by finite distributivity.

domains.original: Section 4.1.1 locates x in R^((h+1)n) with Euclidean blocks. At level i the directions and radial factors use exactly x_i through x_h, and the coefficient space includes all levels.
domains.reconstructed: x is a tuple of h-i+1 vectors in EuclideanSpace R (Fin n). The angular directions are unit on the nonzero branch. Coefficients still occupy the full joint Euclidean direct sum, and the degrees are even integers between 4 and the upper bound inclusive.
domains.evidence: The Lean coordinate j represents source block i+j; Fin(h+1) implies i<=h, so truncated subtraction agrees with h-i. Every suffix extends to a full source location by filling the omitted prefix, on which H_i does not depend. Fin(P+1) plus the parity and lower-bound predicates includes exactly the source degrees, including P; it does not truncate the joint coefficient space to level i.

quantifiers.original: The paper sets n sufficiently large and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32) for its hard family; the §6.2 proof then fixes x before taking a law at any k=0,...,h.
quantifiers.reconstructed: The declaration and reconstruction universally quantify positive n, natural h, an allowed level, and a deterministic trailing location before considering a Gaussian coefficient draw.
quantifiers.evidence: The result specializes to the paper parameter locus. Unit normalization, independent finite Gaussian addition and deterministic scalar multiplication do not use the large-n regime or relation between n and h, so the broader quantification is a disclosed isolated-law generalization. It does not extend the hard-family regularity, admissibility, or asymptotic claims.

assumptions.original: The probability law is the unconditioned standard Gaussian on the joint ordered coefficient direct sum. A fixed location is arbitrary; the paper extends the field by zero when participating blocks vanish.
assumptions.reconstructed: HasLaw specifies stdGaussian on the full flattened Euclidean coefficient space. The location is deterministic; neither nonvanishing of every block nor positivity of the cutoff, measurability, integrability, or Gaussianity of an abstract scalar are extra premises.
assumptions.evidence: The compiled angular sum consumes the actual coefficient Gaussian; its product block law derives independent standard blocks. NormedSpace.normalize equals inverse norm scalar multiplication, and norm one is derived only after the zero-block case split. Both chi denominators are positive because each argument pair sums to 1/20, one argument is positive, and rho is nonnegative everywhere. Lean's totalized division does not change the source value.

conclusion.original: Section 6.2 uses the actual marginal N(0,n C_i(x)^2 v_i) with v_i the sum of squared amplitudes. In the zero-extension or zero-cutoff case the variance is zero.
conclusion.reconstructed: HasLaw gives a.e. measurability and the exact pushforward to gaussianReal of mean zero and variance (n c^2 sum_p a_i,p^2).toNNReal; the decoder spells this as max of the displayed value and zero, then notes equality.
conclusion.evidence: At a zero block, chi(0)=0 by its first numerator, so both H and the specified variance are zero; the proof uses gaussianReal_zero_var and a pointwise equality to zero. With no zero block, gaussianReal_const_mul sends the uncut law to the law scaled by c, including c=0 (e.g. a nonzero block at radius 1). Nonnegativity of n and squares removes the NNReal truncation, verified also by the focused real-variance test.
